financial_summary: Quantum Space, Inc. is a small-cap industrials business with a $782M market cap on $14M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +686% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at -143% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 19% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $15M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, thin -15.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 2.5% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and stock-based comp at 12% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

Cyclicality and capital intensity — order books turn on a dime, and the heavy fixed cost base that creates the moat also magnifies the downturn.
Supply chain reshoring costs and labour shortages — onshoring mandates raise capex requirements while a shrinking skilled-labour pool inflates operating costs.
Tariff and trade-policy exposure — industrial exporters sit squarely in the crosshairs of protectionist policy, and retaliatory tariffs can close markets without warning.
